summary: Column view, all in src/finder. A column after the first now finds its selected item by path when it is read again (`load_column`'s completion looks the selection up as it is when the read ends, then replaces the entries), and when the item is no longer listed it selects nothing, closes the columns after it and makes itself the column in use if a later one was. `load_column` takes an optional item to select (`select: Option<PathBuf>`), which the completion selects with the new window-less `select_in_column_quiet`. The first column does the same when its selected item is no longer among the rows (`sync_root_column`), except while a Nushell filter run is out (`!self.filtering`). What the window selects by itself reaches the columns: `load_listing`'s item and a new folder being named are selected in the first column while it is the column in use and the item isn't selected already (`select_row_in_columns`); a rename reads the further column that lists the item again at once and keeps the item selected there if it was (`renamed_in_columns`, called from `submit_rename`); `files_changed` selects the first of its items that is in the folder of the column in use (`reload_columns_selecting`; `reload_columns` is its empty case). The next item after Move to Trash or Delete Immediately comes from the list the selection is in (`selection_list`: the column in use, or the rows), and `item_after` takes `&[&Path]`. `set_sort` and `set_ascending` read the further columns again. Escape lets go of the item selected in the column in use (`has_selection`, the Columns arm of `clear_selection`, `deselect_in_column`). `select_in_column` keeps its public signature: it gives the files the keyboard, calls `select_in_column_quiet`, and for the first column sets the rows' selection. list.rs `folders_first_changed` calls `reload_columns`. docs/manual.md: the Columns bullet and the Escape row.
changelog: The column view lost track of what was selected. A column after the first remembered its selected item by position, so when its folder changed on disk, or on Refresh, Show Hidden Files or Keep Folders on Top, the highlight moved to a neighbouring item, and Open, Rename, Quick Look and Move to Trash acted on that one. A column now keeps its item selected wherever the item is listed, and when the item is gone, the columns to its right close. A renamed item stays selected, and in a further column shows its new name at once. After Back or Enclosing Folder the folder you came from is selected, and Show in Enclosing Folder selects the item, as in the other views. What a paste, New Folder, New File, Duplicate or Undo brings is selected when it lands in the column you're in, and Move to Trash selects the next item in the first column too. Sort By and Ascending or Descending now sort every column, not only the first. Escape clears the selection in the column view as it does in the others: the active column's item, which closes the columns to its right.
behaviour_changes: A column after the first keeps its selected item when it is read again: after its folder changes on disk (the two-second look), Refresh, Show or Hide Hidden Files, Keep Folders on Top, a change of sort, and a file operation in this tab or another. Before, the highlight, the preview card and Open, Rename, Quick Look and Move to Trash moved to whatever item was at that place in the list. Tested, and pictured (review-selected, review-hidden-shown).

When a column's selected item is gone after it is read again (removed, renamed or moved by another program, or hidden once hidden files are off), nothing is selected there, the columns to its right close, and that column is the one in use if a later one was. Before, another item was highlighted and an empty column for the folder that had gone stayed. By reading: the same happens when the column's folder can't be read at that moment, as on a network volume that drops out: the column is empty, as before, and what was open to its right now closes (before, those columns stayed).

The first column does the same when its selected item is no longer listed: gone, hidden (turning hidden files off while inside a hidden folder closes its columns; probed), or left out by a Nushell filter that has answered. Before, the columns to its right stayed. While a filter is still running, as right after a search ends with a filter on, nothing closes, as before.
Rename in the first column: the item stays selected under its new name, and a renamed folder's column opens again for it. Before, nothing was selected.

Rename in a further column: the column shows the new name at once and the item stays selected where it sorts now; a renamed folder's own column follows. Before, the old name showed until the next look, and then another item could be highlighted. Pictured (review-renamed-dark).

A rename made in the sidebar's tree: a further column that lists the item shows the new name at once and keeps its own selection. When the renamed folder is the one selected in the first column, the columns collapse to the first, with the renamed folder selected and its column opened anew.

Back, Enclosing Folder (Cmd+Up), Show in Enclosing Folder (Cmd+Return or the menus), Go to Folder with a file's path, a click on a file at the end of the path bar, a file dropped where no folder shows, and a file's path given by `fff gui` or a second launch (everything that goes through `reveal_in_place` or `location_changed` with an item) select their item in the first column and scroll to it: a folder with its column beside it, a file with its preview card. Before, nothing was selected while the status bar said 1 selected. In a file chooser, Return after Back therefore chooses the folder you came from, as it does in the other views (by reading). Pictured (review-back).

What a paste, a drop, New File, Duplicate, Make Alias or Symbolic Link, Compress, Extract, Undo or Redo brings is selected when it lands in the column in use. A paste and New File go to the window's folder, so they are selected only while the first column is the one in use. When a further column is in use and the item lands in another column, the columns stay as they are. When the first column is in use with a folder's column open beside it, selecting what came closes that column, as a click on the item would.

New Folder with the first column in use: the new folder is selected (its empty column opens) while it is named and under its name afterwards. Before, the earlier selection stayed. With a further column in use the folder is still made and named in the first column, and the further column keeps its selection and the keyboard afterwards (probed).

Move to Trash and Delete Immediately: in the first column the next item is now selected (before: nothing). In a further column the next item is selected by path, and after the last item the one before it (before: nothing, because the place that was kept was past the end). A next item that is a folder opens its column. An item that could not be trashed stays selected with its column as it was. An item trashed from somewhere other than the column in use (the sidebar's tree, a drag to the Trash) selects a next item only when it was listed in the column in use.

Sort By, Ascending and Descending sort every column at once. Before, only the first; the others at their next reading. A folder selected in a column keeps its own column open through the sort (probed).

Escape lets go of the item selected in the column in use and closes the columns to its right. In the first column the other views' selection goes too, so the list shows nothing selected afterwards. With the first column in use Escape also clears that selection when no column shows any of it, as after Select All or after choosing the column view with items selected, so the status bar's count goes as it did before this change (the review's fix). With a further column in use and nothing selected there, Escape does nothing, or cancels a chooser, and the earlier columns' grey selection stays; the status bar then still counts the first column's item. Before, Escape cleared only the other views' selection: nothing changed in the columns, only the status bar's count. Pictured (review-escape).

With the change that landed just before it (stale-previews-and-cancel, 52e7de4): a reading of the column in use asks for the preview of the item that is selected there afterwards, which is now the same item or the one the window selected, never a neighbour. By reading: Quick Look, when open, then follows the item the window selects in a further column, such as the next one after a move to the Trash, and after Back the folder that is selected has its item count read once in the background, which the column view doesn't show.

Manual: the Columns bullet says the sort applies to every column, that an item stays selected when its column is sorted another way or read again, and that the columns to its right close once it is gone. The Escape row says what Escape clears in columns.

The three ways this was most likely to hurt, each held against the code. (1) A destructive key landing on an item the user didn't choose: an index and its entries are only ever replaced together (`sync_root_column`, `load_column`'s completion), `active_column` is clamped wherever columns close, and when a selected item goes nothing is selected in its place, so Cmd+Backspace then does nothing. The window now selects the next item after a move to the Trash in the first column too, as the other views always did. (2) Losing one's place: the columns close only when the selected item is really not listed. The one case where it is missing for a moment, a filter that hasn't answered, is guarded. A column whose folder can't be read counts as not listing anything (behaviour change 3), as the window's own folder does when it can't be read. (3) The keyboard taken out of the column in use by something that ends later: nothing is selected in a column other than the one in use, except the renamed item in the column where it was selected, and the choice is made when the operation ends, not when it starts.

For briefs still to come.
- view-switch-keeps-selection: the window-less helper is `select_in_column_quiet(col, ix, cx) -> bool`, and for a row of the first column `select_row_in_columns(ix, cx)`, which does nothing unless the column view shows and the first column is in use, leaves an item that is selected already as it is, and doesn't touch the rows' selection. In `set_view_mode`, after `self.columns.clear(); self.sync_root_column();`, call `self.select_row_in_columns(ix, cx)` with the row `primary_entry` would pick. Escape reads the column's selection in this view (`has_selection`), and with the first column in use also the rows' selection; the Escape test's block that selects in the list and then chooses columns asserts nothing in between and holds either way.
- select-all-perf: `item_after` takes `&[&Path]`; `selection_list()` builds that list once per move to the Trash or delete (the rows, or the column in use). `load_listing`'s found-branch has one more call, `select_row_in_columns(first, cx)`. Select All in the column view still selects only in the rows' selection, which no column shows; Escape in the first column clears it.
- filter-stale-keep-set: `sync_root_column` closes the columns only while no filter run is out (`!self.filtering`), because until the filter answers the rows are cut by what it kept of the last ones. With a filter on, ending a search or renaming the first column's selected folder still takes the first column's highlight (the row is missing for that moment) and leaves the further columns, as before this change. If your change removes the moment, the guard can go; the second half of the_columns_close_for_what_a_filter_leaves_out_once_it_has_answered keeps passing.
- stale-rows-on-place-change, idle-redraw-after-search: `select_row_in_columns` relies on `rebuild_rows` having run `sync_root_column` just before in the same completion (a row's index is its index in the first column). Keep that order in `load_listing`'s completion.
- files-changed-off-thread: `files_changed` keeps the unfiltered `select` and ends with `reload_columns_selecting(&select, cx)`; the column to select in is the one in use at that moment. Keep both when the stat calls move off the thread.
- new-item-in-hidden-row: `add_and_rename` has one more line, `self.select_row_in_columns(ix, cx)`, after `self.selection.select_only(ix)`. In the column view a new folder is selected in the first column while it is named, and its empty column opens.
- quick-look-empty-state: `clear_selection` in the column view lets go of the item selected in the column in use (and of the rows' selection for the first column); in the other views it is as it was, so your tests, which select in the list, are not touched. `item_after` has the new signature.
- preview-page-keys, quick-look-empty-state: `select_in_column` and `select_in_column_quiet` still don't call `selection_changed` (a folder's preview isn't wanted for every folder clicked through), so Quick Look doesn't follow a click or Page Down in the column view with `ensure_pdf` or `ensure_explore`. A reading of the column in use does call it (52e7de4).
- inactive-selection-colour, icon-tile-hit-target, type-select-space, go-to-folder-keyboard, split-active-pane, tab-drop-and-close, restore-session-tabs, preview-card-height, image-preview-details, table-preview-column-widths, context-menus-fit: independent. `render_column_row` is not touched by this change.

Found, not fixed (there before, outside this brief).
- A right-click on a row that is already selected in a column that isn't the one in use (the grey row of an earlier column) opens the menu for the item of the column in use: probed, the menu over the folder Projects read Cut "b.txt", and its Move to Trash would have trashed b.txt. The row's right-press handler in `render_column_row` selects only when `p.selected != Some(ix)`. It should also make the column the one in use when it isn't (`|| col != this.active_column`, or what Left does). Worth a brief of its own: it is the wrong-item fault this change fixes, by another way in.
- The status bar's "N of M selected" counts the rows' selection in the column view, not the column's: after Move to Trash in a further column it reads "15 items" with an item selected, after Escape in a further column it still counts the first column's item, and after choosing columns with items selected in the list it counts items no column shows.
- Select All, and Return or Down from an empty search field, select only in the rows' selection in the column view, where nothing shows it.
- A press on another row during an inline rename that was refused selects that row in the column view (`select_in_column` has no `renaming` check as `click_row` has).
- Columns after the first don't read the dates items were last opened (`load_column` has no `read_last_opened`) or folders' sizes from the index, so those two sorts differ from the first column. `if sort.key == SortKey::LastOpened { entries.iter_mut().for_each(FileEntry::read_last_opened) }` before the sort in `load_column` would do for the first.
- Paste, New Folder and New File always go to the window's folder, even with a further column in use. Finder puts them in the column in use.
- Back from a folder opened two levels down (a double-click in a further column) selects nothing, in every view: the folder gone into isn't listed in the folder Back leads to.
- Seen by the implementer in a random walk: Undo of a Duplicate while the window is inside the copy leaves "Can't open this folder".
- Trashing a folder from the sidebar's tree while the first column or the list has another item selected moves the selection to the item after the folder (`item_after` over the list the selection is in). There before in the list; the first column now does the same.
- `set_view_mode` leaves `self.columns` as they were when another view is chosen, so Refresh, hidden files, a file operation and now a change of sort read those folders again in the background until the window goes somewhere else. Harmless, and wasted.
